mappings.note: Translation v1 describes David going to En-Gedi *before* Saul's return. OSMAIN starts with Saul returning and then being told David is there (v1). The event of David arriving first is missing in OSMAIN.
Translation v2 covers the report to Saul. OSMAIN v1 contains this report but also includes Saul's return context which is split in translation.
Both describe Saul taking 3000 men to the rocks of Ziph (Steingeit-klippene).
Both describe Saul entering the cave for his needs while David is inside.
Translation v2 ends with 'coupa t' (cut). OSMAIN v4 contains the full speech and the action of cutting. Translation splits this verse.
Both describe David's heart smiting him after cutting the corner.
David's speech forbidding harm to the Lord's anointed.
Men held back, Saul leaves the cave.
David calls out, bows, and prostrates himself.
David asks why Saul listens to those saying he seeks evil.
Translation v11 ends abruptly ('ma main'). OSMAIN v10 contains the full sentence about sparing him.
Translation v12 ends abruptly ('d'inju'). OSMAIN v11 contains the full sentence about no evil in his heart.
David calls for judgment and states his hand will not touch Saul.
Proverb about evil coming from the wicked; David's hand will not touch Saul.
David asks who the King is pursuing (a dead dog/flea).
David calls for judgment and deliverance.
Saul recognizes David's voice and weeps.
Saul admits David is more righteous; good for evil.
Saul acknowledges the sparing and asks for reward.
Rhetorical question about letting an enemy go; blessing requested.
Saul acknowledges David will be king.
Saul asks for an oath not to destroy his lineage.
David swears; Saul leaves; David goes to the stronghold.
